publications.title: Quark dipole operators in the gradient-flow scheme at NNLO QCD
publications.summary: Conversion factors for the dimension-five QCD operator basis from the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ to the gradient-flow scheme are presented through NNLO in the strong coupling. In the CP-even sector, the results are provided for general quark masses and arbitrary flavor content of the operators. Specifically, this concerns the quark CMDM operator and its mixing with lower-dimensional QCD operators. In the massless case, our results immediately apply to the quark chromoelectric dipole operator. As a by-product, we also determine missing entries in the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ anomalous dimension matrix of the CMDM operator to NNLO QCD.

publications.title: From Resonance Properties to High-Energy Behavior: The $R$ Ratio from Lattice QCD
publications.summary: We investigate resonance properties and inclusive spectral behavior through Bayesian reconstruction of the $R$-ratio from Euclidean lattice correlators near the physical pion mass. Without additional Gaussian smearing, the reconstructed spectrum already captures the smooth high-energy behavior observed in experiment. Direct integration of the $ρ$ peak determines $f_ρ$ with approximately $1\%$ statistical precision and close agreement with the experimental reference, providing access to resonance properties without resolving individual finite-volume levels. With a common Gaussian width of $σ=0.6$~GeV, the lattice and experimental $R$-ratios show good overall agreement over $0.25$--$2.50$~GeV. Comparisons among ensembles with spatial extents up to approximately $10$~fm demonstrate that finite-volume effects can be controlled across these complementary observables. These results demonstrate a unified framework for studying resonance and inclusive physics from lattice QCD, with potential applications to other hadronic channels, inclusive decay rates, and hadronic tensors.

publications.title: Optimized solver algorithms for computing $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$
publications.summary: Estimating the trace of the inverse of a large quark matrix is a longstanding problem in lattice QCD. The standard approach is Hutchinson's method, which uses random noise vectors to estimate the trace to a desired statistical tolerance. Each noise vector $b$ requires solving a system of linear equations $Ax = b$. In this work, we introduce a new class of Krylov solvers for this task, called Twin methods. Twin methods generate the Krylov polynomial once then reuse it on all other right-hand sides. This reduces the number of basic linear algebra operations in the algorithm and therefore lowers the trace computation time. We apply the Twin approach to BiCG and BiCGStab and test them on lattice QCD matrices of varying size and in a range of computing contexts. We also present a more economical estimation of $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$ which implements a polynomial approximation of $A^{-1}$ and a singular value deflation. In this scheme, the solvers are applied to only a few noise vectors, and the remainder are treated by the polynomial and the deflation. In our tests, the polynomial approximation combined with the deflation yield a 17-fold speedup in the time required to compute the trace over standard Hutchinson's method.

publications.title: Review of Pion and Nucleon Gluon Parton Distribution Functions from Lattice QCD
publications.summary: Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of PDFs directly from lattice QCD. Among the available approaches, the large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) and pseudo-PDF frameworks have emerged as the most widely used methods and have produced the majority of lattice determinations of parton distributions. These developments have sparked rapid progress in first-principles studies of the $x$-dependent structure of hadrons, including gluon PDFs of the nucleon and pseudoscalar mesons. In this review, we summarize recent advances in lattice QCD calculations of gluon PDFs {using the LaMET and pseudo-PDF methods}, discuss the current status and impacts of these developments, and highlight the remaining challenges and future opportunities.

publications.title: Positivity, Noise, and Cones
publications.summary: As a consequence of causality, Euclidean-time correlation functions in quantum field theory are subject to constraints in the form of positivity conditions on certain Hankel matrices. Such conditions define convex conic structures. Correlation functions computed numerically using Monte Carlo techniques generally contain statistical fluctuations that violate the positivity conditions. This work describes a projection procedure, based on the convex conic geometry induced by the positivity conditions and a statistical covariance matrix, that can be used to restore positivity, providing a unique decomposition for noisy correlators into causal and acausal components. In contrast to previous literature, this work explicitly leverages the conic structure and not just the convex nature of the causal space. The projection can be computed using primal-dual interior-point methods. Constrained projection gives rise to observable-specific frequentist confidence intervals for smeared spectral densities in the causal bootstrap of [Phys. Rev. D 114, 074510 (2026)]. Analytic results are supported with numerical examples.
